SEC Charges Nimbus Lending and Founder Mark Ellery With Defrauding Retail Crypto Investors

Published 2026-10-06 15:00 UTC

Washington D.C., Oct. 6, 2026 The Securities and Exchange Commission today charged Nimbus Lending LLC and its founder and CEO, Mark Ellery, with defrauding more than 90,000 retail investors through the unregistered offer and sale of crypto asset securities through its Yield Vault program.

According to the SEC's complaint, Nimbus raised approximately $1.2 billion by promising returns of up to 14 percent, which it claimed were generated by low-risk lending to institutional borrowers. In reality, the complaint alleges, Nimbus used new investor deposits to pay returns to earlier investors and Ellery diverted more than $40 million for personal use.

The SEC's complaint, filed in federal district court in Manhattan, charges Nimbus and Ellery with violating the registration and antifraud provisions of the federal securities laws and seeks permanent injunctions, disgorgement and civil penalties.

The SEC's complaint alleges that from 2022 through 2025, Nimbus and Ellery raised more than $1.2 billion from retail investors through its interest-bearing crypto accounts, which the SEC alleges were securities offered and sold without registration. Nimbus represented that customer assets would be lent only to creditworthy institutional borrowers on an overcollateralized basis.

In reality, according to the complaint, Nimbus transferred approximately $400 million of customer assets to a trading firm owned and controlled by Ellery, which used the assets for speculative trading. Nimbus allegedly concealed these transfers from investors and continued to tout the safety of its lending program even as losses mounted.

The complaint, filed in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, charges Nimbus and Ellery with violating the registration and antifraud provisions of the Securities Act of 1933 and the antifraud provisions of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The SEC seeks permanent injunctions, disgorgement with prejudgment interest, civil penalties, and an officer-and-director bar against Ellery.

The SEC's investigation is continuing. The SEC encourages investors who believe they were harmed by Nimbus to contact the agency. Investors can learn more about the risks of crypto asset lending products through the SEC's Office of Investor Education and Advocacy.

Nimbus froze customer withdrawals in 2025, leaving approximately 90,000 retail investors unable to access their crypto assets. The SEC alleges the crypto lender and its founder misled savers about the safety of the Nimbus lending program and about the $1.2 billion it raised, while Ellery's trading firm lost much of the customer money.
